messages:
maria: Heads up — during today's priv-deploy hardening window (onprem eu-2) we started seeing KMS decrypt failures from model-serving pods after I applied the key-rotation patch. Appears as 403 PERMISSION_DENIED in keystore logs. 09:03 UTC
will: Can you paste a sample audit line?
maria: `2026-03-24T09:02:54Z keystore svc=keystore-pod pod=serve-12 decrypt err=PERMISSION_DENIED key=projects/_/locations/global/keyRings/rw/cryptoKeys/serve-key caller=serviceAccount:node-sa`
devops-raj: Did the rotation change key version or IAM policy? Two failure modes: key disabled/rotation not synced OR service account lost kms.cryptoKeyDecrypter role.
tanya: I pushed a key-rotation that also updated key ring, but I did not touch IAM. I did, however, tighten PodSecurityPolicy and removed hostPath access for infra nodes earlier in the window.
keystore-bot: ALERT keystore/serve-12 returned KMS 403 x18 in 5m, cached decrypt fallbacks exhausted. 
auditor-bot: KMS audit: detected 'cryptoKeys.get' succeeded for control-plane but 'cryptoKeys.decrypt' returned PERMISSION_DENIED for principal serviceAccount:node-sa at 09:02:54 UTC.
will: Interesting — audit shows decrypt rejected, but get succeeded. That usually means the key exists but permissions on the cryptoKeyVersion or key-level IAM may have changed.
devops-raj: Can an affected pod reach the internal KMS endpoint? Try `nc -vz kms.internal.redwood 443` from the pod.
maria: nc times out from serve-12. From bastion it connects. NetworkPolicy ingress/egress? We have a restrictive egress NP applied to 'serve' namespace last week.
keystore-bot: NP applied: egressToInfraOnly selector=namespace:infra denies other egress. Current netpol: apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1, kind: NetworkPolicy, name: egressToInfraOnly; egress -> to namespaceSelector matchLabels: infra; ports 443/TCP.
maria: I can confirm a two-fold issue: 1) key rotation accidentally set the key's IAM to exclude node-sa (operator error) and 2) egress netpol prevents pods from reaching the revocation-check endpoint, so stale cached ACLs remain in memory causing confusing audits.
tanya: To fix fast: I rolled back IAM binding change to add roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to serviceAccount:node-sa and added an egress exception for namespace serve to allow kms.internal.redwood:443 and 10.210.0.0/24. Did a rolling restart of serving pods.
will: Confirmed decrypts resumed. Still: we should treat key rotation as an operation that requires coordinated IAM and network preflight.
devops-raj: Action items: 1) Add preflight checklist that verifies key ACLs and IAM bindings pre- and post-rotation; 2) Add an automated CI netpol simulation that runs `nc`/curl to kms from a pod before promotion; 3) Harden the keystore agent to surface clear error codes (KS-ERR-403 -> runbook link); 4) Add KMS IAM audit alert for mass principal removals.
keystore-bot: Incident INC-2026-08 opened by maria; severity P2.
ops-bot: Noted. Scheduling 30m postmortem tomorrow.
maria: Also, follow-up vulnerability triage: the PSP tightening caused nodes to drop a kubelet CSI mount used by the keystore agent to read cached key material — add to postmortem.
will: For isolation guarantees we should document minimum egress allowlist for priv-deploy (kms endpoints, metadata, iaas-proxy) and add them to priv-deploy helm chart values.
devops-raj: I'll own the PR to add the CI netpol-e2e preflight and a canary process: apply netpol in staging->canary->prod with automated smokeers.
maria: Closing interim: mitigation worked, incident created. Please attach logs to INC-2026-08 and tag audit leads. :thumbsup:
